note: Cashless means cards and bank balances instead of notes and coins. The push is to retire physical cash so every payment sits on an account someone can see, freeze, or program.
A CBDC is a central-bank digital currency: state money on a database, not bitcoin. It can be identified, limited, and switched off. "Going cashless" in this verse looks straight at that design.
A stack that stands only while nobody pulls a card. The line is the cashless setup: it holds until one rail, one bank, or one rule change folds it.
Derelict means abandoned. The graveyard is the tokens that are not bitcoin, left after the hype. "Why not any others?" just waved them off. This is where they sit.
The Mona Lisa stands in for work that took years. You do not get it without effort. The line is aimed at a market that offers a huge multiple for showing up.

Feds: federal agents. The thing they can do, in this bar, is take the necklace. Civil forfeiture lets the state seize property — cash, cars, jewelry — often without the owner being convicted of a crime.
The necklace is the small, specific version of a seizure. Not a fine. The object itself. Paired with "the feds," it is forfeiture told as a stick-up.
Gluttonous excess is more than enough, taken anyway. The next line's death grip "suffocates": too much hold, not enough air. One idea from both sides.
The dollar still ranks first in the reflex. "Everybody falls for it" is the habit of measuring a life in the unit that is being issued. The bill stays the priority even in a song about leaving cash.
Software slang: what looks broken is the design. The salesman uses it straight — convince the buyer the flaw was intentional. In a lot of token launches, the dump was the feature.

phrase: ICO had a hella large liquidity
note: An ICO is an initial coin offering: sell a new token to the public before it really trades. "Hella large liquidity" means the pool looked deep. Depth that insiders can pull is not the same as a market.
300x is three hundred times your money, the pitch. A pump is the rise that makes the multiple look real. The next bars are the exit: dump, then liquidate the pools.
A DEX is a decentralized exchange. Pools are the piles of tokens that set the price. Liquidating them pulls that inventory so the price collapses after the insiders are out.

phrase: the SEC won't tighten up nothing
note: The SEC is the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The line is a shrug: the odds they arrive in time. "Maybe you got scammed" is the correction to "you did not get scammed," one bar later.
Two rooms, and the bar refuses to merge them. Crypto vegas is the token arcade. Bitcoin is the other status: a monetary network, not a table.

A Faraday cage blocks electromagnetic fields. People use one so a hardware wallet cannot be reached remotely. A microwave is a metal box that roughly blocks signal and will also cook the device. Bad opsec in a costume.

A stop-loss sells when price falls to a level you set, to cap the damage. "10% negated" is that band. Swing trades are positions held across days, not seconds. The bar is the trader's checklist, not a promise.
To orange-pill someone is to convince them of bitcoin — the red pill, turned Bitcoin orange. "Prescribe them 3 of them" treats the glossary like a dose.
TOS: terms of service. The platform rules. They are how a host tells a monetary argument to leave. The stickers and the ban in the next lines are the enforcement.
"Not financial advice," pasted on a post so a rant is not treated as a regulated recommendation. The song hears the sticker as a muzzle. It still does not stop the ban.
A shadow ban hides you without saying you are banned. The account still looks open. Reach drops. "Cancel the man" is the loud version of the same move.

BRICS is the bloc — Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, and later others — often pitched as a counterweight to the dollar. The lyric spells it BRICs. The line is the choice those "scholars" offer: their bloc, or the dollar.
The inside version: the feed, the terms, what you are allowed to say. "If insides mind control" is slanged, and the meaning is the narrative. The next line takes the same idea outdoors.
The external half of the previous bar. Sanctions, seizures, and actual war, set against the version that happens on a platform. One pair: story, then force.
